newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-UNITED FANS HIT BY ANTI-RIOT PELLETS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNITED FANS HIT BY ANTI-RIOT PELLETS.

text.p: Several Manchester United fans were being treated in hospital early on Thursday after police opened fire with anti-riot pellets during disturbances at the European Cup quarter-final second leg tie with Porto on Wednesday night.
Officials at the Sao Jorge hospital said six or seven English fans had been brought in from the Das Antas stadium with plastic pellet wounds, including one supporter who had been hit in the head.
"They were hit...but no vital organs were damaged," Doctor Luis Aguiar told Reuters, adding that all the injured were expected to be able to leave hospital within the following few hours.
Police had battled to restrain a crowd of United fans trying to leave the ground as the match, in which the English champions clinched a place in the European Cup semifinals, was drawing to a close.
The game ended 0-0 but United coasted through on aggregate, having trounced Porto 4-0 in the first leg in Manchester.
The fans had ignored a police warning that they should remain in the ground for at least 45 minutes after the game to give local Porto supporters time to clear the stadium.

Witnesses said the police also used batons and tear gas to force back the dozens of fans converging on the exit. Police said some 15 officers were also slightly injured in the clashes, but no arrests were made.
"It was a disgrace, they opened fire on us. I have five wounds," one United fan told Reuters.
It was the second incident of the night involving the visiting supporters.
Earlier, 20 United fans were hurt, including three who were taken to hospital. Most had cuts and bruises after clashing with riot police in a disturbance outside the stadium.
A spokeswoman for the British consulate told BBC Radio Five Live that all the supporters involved were Manchester United fans.
"They were stuck outside the ground and upset they could not get in after the match started," she said.
The problem appears to have arisen after they were found to have tickets reserved for areas where Porto fans were allocated.
"We cannot confirm that there were any forged tickets," she said.
About 10,000 fans had followed their team to Portugal for the match.
It was reported that around 200 United fans were involved in the fracas before the game and were told they would not be allowed in as their tickets were forged.
However, room was later found for them inside the stadium.
